candidates.label: expectedPrognosis
candidates.comment: An expected prognosis relation between a medical condition and its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called: anticipated outcome, predicted course, outlook. Examples: "Common Cold" expected prognosis "Full recovery within a week", "Type 2 Diabetes" expected prognosis "Manageable with lifestyle changes and medication", "Stage 4 Cancer" expected prognosis "Poor, with limited treatment options".

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: estimatedCost
candidates.comment: An estimated cost relation between a how-to instruction or supply and the monetary amount or text representing its approximate cost. Also called "approximate cost", "projected expense", "expected price". Examples: "HowTo 'Build a Shelf' estimatedCost '$50'", "HowToSupply 'Wood' estimatedCost '20 USD'", "Project 'Renovation' estimatedCost 'Approx. $10,000'".

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: expectedArrivalUntil
candidates.comment: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: includedComposition

Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart

Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: recipeIngredient
candidates.comment: A recipe ingredient relation between a recipe and the components, often with quantities, required for its preparation. Also called ingredients for, recipe components, required items. Examples: "A cake recipe includes recipe ingredients '2 cups flour'.", "A salad recipe lists recipe ingredients 'lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber'.", "A stew recipe requires recipe ingredients 'beef, potatoes, carrots'."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: containsSeason

Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

candidates.label: containsPlace

Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: ingredients

Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: muscleAction
candidates.comment: A description of the movement generated by a muscle. Also called muscle function, muscle movement, action of muscle. Examples: "Biceps Brachii muscleAction 'flexion of elbow'", "Triceps Brachii muscleAction 'extension of elbow'", "Deltoid muscleAction 'abduction of shoulder'".

candidates.label: nerveMotor

Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". candidates.label: intensity
candidates.comment: A physical exertion measure relation between an exercise plan and the degree of force or effort involved in the exercise. Also called exertion level, effort level, vigor, strenuousness. Examples: An exercise plan has an intensity of 'moderate'. A running plan specifies an intensity of '150 bpm'. A weightlifting plan has an intensity of 'high'.

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission

Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: source

Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.
